overall.note: All continuous milestones reached reported web green, and both full replays verified invariants. Integrated authorization, assets and offline infrastructure helped substantially; restrictive query bounds and complex authority reconciliation prevented a consistently direct build (final-report.md; essay.md).

setup_and_docs.note: M1's scaffold, built-in password auth and generated types worked quickly; published guides supported the entire build. M6 session TTL details and M8 compaction recovery guidance remained incomplete (diary.md; essay.md).

data_modeling.note: Unique constraints and maintained counts expressed the core model well. Quarry's limited expression vocabulary and certified bounds required narrower projections, compact counters and staged designs (diary.md M2–M3, M6, M8).

authorization.note: Membership rules composed directly with delivery and assets. Removal/rejoin receipt checks, logout revocation and private-chat digest exclusions passed builder proofs; independent holdout grading remains unavailable (diary.md M3; run-log.md M6/M8; final-report.md).

queries_and_live.note: Live feeds, expiring typing channels and indexed search were direct, but certification forced one-message enriched API pages and client merging for 1,000-chat search (diary.md M2–M6; final-report.md).

writes_and_transactions.note: Idempotent set-state mutations, unique DMs, server-time windows and resumable replay worked; both 167,244-action replays verified invariants. Durable create bindings required pure inserts, constraining mutation structure (diary.md M3–M6; final-report.md).

offline_sync.note: The SDK supplied retained reads and a durable FIFO outbox; M6/M8 web ordering and convergence passed. Compaction recovery needed an additional authoritative observer; native restart behavior remains unproven (diary.md M6/M8; essay.md; final-report.md).

media_assets.note: Typed asset arguments avoided separate upload plumbing. Cell ownership and per-recipient consumption supported deletion and view-once refusal, with actual media verification; protected avatar rendering required a blob bridge (diary.md M1–M5; final-report.md).

background_work.note: Presence-driven push, row timers and autonomous digest/restart proofs worked. Certified bounds required staged digest counters and jobs; the public scheduler lacked direct calendar dispatch, using installation-relative cadence after UTC boundaries (diary.md M5–M8; final-report.md).

client_integration.note: Generated hooks, auth stores and Expo providers helped integration. Aggregate reads required an online client alongside durable messaging, observed queries lacked a direct refresh handle, and the scaffold lacked Router navigation (diary.md M1/M8; essay.md).

diagnostics_dev_loop.note: Bounds and schema diagnostics identified limits and guided corrections; published guides and generated types supplied useful fixes. Supplemental testing certified 57 operations, while missing authored seeds and journeys blocked derived checks (run-log.md; final-report.md).

scale_and_limits.note: Both replays verified invariants and final 3× ratios passed, but two strict midpoint rules failed. Supplementary hub search required 1,157 requests; cold sync took 55.869 seconds with approximately 637 MB peak heap (final-report.md; run-log.md).

operations.note: Idempotent seeds, reviewed successor migrations, isolated replays and public inspection worked. A parked-job count lacked a usable public mapping; the internal test owner exposed neither PID nor port override. M7 evolution remains unobserved (final-report.md; diary.md M2).

snapback2.verdict: Snapback 2 fit Clique's authorization, media and durable messaging well, while query bounds and client synchronization required substantial additional design.
snapback2.would_use_again_for: I would use it again for messengers and collaborative apps needing durable offline writes and revocable media, with teams prepared to design around certified query bounds.

notes: The strongest benefits were integrated membership delivery, policy-controlled assets, the SDK-owned outbox and a real scheduled digest that survived restart (diary.md M3–M8; final-report.md).
The principal platform costs were constrained enriched reads, per-chat search merging, staged digest computation and incomplete refresh and calendar scheduling surfaces (essay.md; final-report.md).
The M2 run-log explicitly labels the 1,000-follow closure refusal snapback2-defect; its penalty is limited because the required 500-follow query compiled.
Agent-error, environment and ambiguous incident costs are excluded, including the mistaken membership cap, application custody regressions, Linux simulator absence and owner timeout (run-log.md).

The supplied evidence reports builder web greens and successful invariant replays, with two strict scale midpoint misses; native restart behavior, M7 evolution and external holdout correctness are not established (final-report.md; run-record.json).
